title: Technical Overadvances Drawn Before a New Certificate Is Verified — Operating Lines of Credit
content:
On the Operating Lines of Credit, an advance drawn while the association had not yet verified a newly delivered borrowing base certificate is treated as a technical overadvance, and its overadvance fee is charged at a share of itself.

## Rule

Counting from the date the line's most recent certificate — the one with the latest as-of date — was received, that received date itself being day 0, the fee figured so far is:

- **multiplied by 0.5** when the advance was drawn no more than 3 calendar days after that receipt;
- **multiplied by 0.75** when it was drawn more than 3 but no more than 10 calendar days after that receipt;
- **charged whole** when it was drawn more than 10 days after that receipt, or before the certificate was received.

The share multiplies the fee before it is rounded to cents; the fee is rounded only after this share is applied. The date the advance was drawn is its effective date in the line's transaction history; the received date is the one recorded on the certificate.

## Day count table (hypothetical certificate received on 10 April)

| Advance drawn | Days after receipt | Fee charged |
|---|---|---|
| 10 April | 0 | 0.5 of the fee |
| 13 April | 3 | 0.5 of the fee |
| 14 April | 4 | 0.75 of the fee |
| 20 April | 10 | 0.75 of the fee |
| 21 April | 11 | The whole fee |
| 8 April | before receipt | The whole fee |

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A fee figured at USD 802.50 on an advance drawn 2 days after the certificate was received is charged at 0.5 of itself, USD 401.25.
